title: Nvidia Earnings Could Trigger a Chilling Reality Check For $1 Trillion AI Boom, Says Analyst: 'Biggest Thing I Am Watching...' (UPDATED)

content_html:
Editor's Note: The story has been refreshed with the latest market price action and a revised headline.

Nvidia Corp.'s (NASDAQ:NVDA) fiscal second-quarter results could offer the clearest indication yet of whether the massive AI infrastructure spending cycle is still accelerating or nearing a peak.

Nvidia Earnings Put AI Infrastructure Boom to the Test

Nvidia is set to report results Wednesday after the bell, with Wall Street expecting roughly $92 billion in revenue, while the company has guided to $91 billion, plus or minus 2%.

Daniel Newman, CEO of The Futurum Group, told Benzinga that Nvidia is the "cleanest test" of whether AI infrastructure demand has actually peaked.

Newman expects revenue could reach $94 billion to $95 billion, potentially exceeding Nvidia's guidance, with October-quarter revenue potentially climbing toward $107 billion to $108 billion and eventually topping $110 billion.

If Nvidia continues delivering accelerating revenue while keeping gross margins in the mid-70% range, Newman said it would be difficult to argue that the underlying compute cycle is already rolling over.

Read Also:Jensen Huang Once Revealed He 'Wasn't A Particularly Good Kid' but One That 'Just Turned Out Good' — Here's Something Today's Nvidia CEO Knew Even at a Young Age

Nvidia Hyperscaler Growth Faces Its Next Big Test

Beyond the headline revenue number, Newman said, "The biggest thing I am watching beyond the headline beat is the Hyperscale versus ACIE split."

He said Nvidia's decision to break out Data Center demand between major cloud and internet companies and its broader AI Cloud, Industrial and Enterprise customer base gives investors a clearer view of whether AI demand is expanding beyond the industry's biggest buyers.

Hyperscalers such as Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT), Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN), Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) and Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) have driven much of the AI infrastructure boom.

U.S. hyperscalers are expected to spend roughly $916 billion on capital expenditures over the next 12 months, with consensus estimates projecting that figure to rise to nearly $1.2 trillion the year after.

Newman believes the next phase could become more durable if ACIE growth accelerates rapidly, signaling that enterprises, industrial companies, sovereign customers and neoclouds are taking on more AI compute demand.

Strong Nvidia Earnings May Not Mean Higher NVDA Stock

Still, Newman cautioned that an earnings beat alone may not send Nvidia shares higher.
